CITY OF ALHAMBRA

NOTICE OF THE REGULAR MEETING OF THE ALHAMBRA YOUTH COMMISSION

  September 13, 2022

  (NOTICE NO. N2M22-104)

  CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY NOTICE

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the regular meeting of the Alhambra Youth Commission
Meeting will be held on Tuesday, September 13, 2022, commencing at 6:00 P.M. video conference.

Consistent with AB 361, the Alhambra Youth Commission meeting will not be physically open to
the public, although the public may participate by video conference or teleconference.
To watch and listen to the meeting: To maximize public safety while still maintaining transparency and
public access, members of the public can participate by using Zoom Webinar as follows:
Zoom Webinar direct link:
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/81684207143?pwd=Z1lmanBTSVdZZWxtbEVZaDhCSzNVQT09
Webinar ID: 816 8420 7143 Passcode: Commission

Or by telephone by dialing 888-475-4499 (Toll Free) or 833-548-0276 (Toll Free) or 833-548-0282 (Toll
Free) or 877-853-5257 (Toll Free) or 1-253-215-8782 or 1-346-248-7799 or 1-253-215-8782 or 1-646-
558-8656 or 1-301-715-8592 or 1-312-626-6799 and entering Webinar ID: 816 8420 7143 and
Passcode: Commission. Please Note: All members of the public calling or logging into the meeting will
be muted so that the meeting can proceed.
For those wishing to speak on an agenda or non-agendized item, you have 3 options for participation:
1) Pre-register to speak: Please email Rosalyn Rojas at rrojas@cityofalhambra.org by 5:00 p.m. prior
to the meeting with the item number you wish to speak on and the phone number you will use when
calling or the name you will use when logging into the meeting. You should then call or log into the
meeting at least 10 minutes prior to its start time. Staff will unmute you and announce you when it is
your time to speak. You will have five minutes to speak, unless that time is adjusted by the Recreation
Supervisor. If you do not have access to a computer, please call 626-570-3209 to request public
comment.
2) “Raise your hand”: For those members of the public that wish to speak but did not make a request
via email as described above, such members of the public may speak by using the “Raise Hand” function
during the public comments portion, if on Zoom. Staff will unmute you and announce you when it is your
time to speak. If participating via telephone, the Mayor will ask anyone participating by telephone if they
would like to speak after asking those on Zoom. Staff will unmute telephone callers and you may state
you wish to speak.
3) Emailed comments to be read into the record: As an alternative to speaking during the meeting,
you can email your comments to the Recreation Supervisor at rrojas@cityofalhambra.org by no later
than 5:00 p.m. on September 13, 2022 to ensure that the Recreation Supervisor has time to print the
emails prior to the beginning of the meeting. Comments will then be read into the record by the
Recreation Supervisor, with a maximum allowance of 5 minutes per individual comment, subject to
the Recreation Supervisor’s discretion. If a comment is received after 5:00 p.m. but before the
conclusion of the meeting based upon its time stamp, the comment will still be included as a part of
the record of the meeting but will not be read into the record.
Any member of the public who needs accommodations or who needs their comments translated
should email or call the Recreation Supervisor at rrojas@cityofalhambra.org or (626) 570-3209 who will
use their best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations to provide as much accessibility as
possible while also maintaining public safety.

We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.

If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and
give it to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If
you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will
be heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Commission
on a subject which does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or community service,
you may make your presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised that the Commission
cannot, under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on any item which does
not appear on the agenda.

When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make
your statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

Minutes
  Alhambra Youth Commission
  September 13, 2022

The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:05 PM on September 13, 2022 at Almansor
Park, 800 S. Almansor Street, Alhambra, CA.

Commission Members Present: I. Lam, J. Quach, N. Quach, A. Taing, and M. Webster,
C. Yu
Commission Members Absent: D. Andrade, J. Cooper, A. Gutierrez, T. Hernandez, and Z. Oliva
Also present: Deputy Director - Brie Houghton, Supervisor - Rosalyn Rojas and Coordinator - Frank Reyes

Flag Salute

Approval of Minutes
President N. Quach moved to approve the Minutes of May 10, 2022. Adjourned Regular Meeting.
Motioned by Commissioner M. Webster and Seconded by President N. Quach

Staff Report
Supervisor Rosalyn Rojas welcomed the new Commissioners and asked them to introduce
themselves. Commissioners I. Lam, A. Taing, and C. Yu introduced themselves and shared what
they looked forward to as being part of the Youth Commission. Supervisor Rojas addressed the
issue of communication with the Commission in light of not having a meeting for 3 months and
not receiving responses to emails. She suggested using an Application called GroupMe.
Coordinator Frank Reyes asked the Commissioners what methods of communication and or
Applications they currently use with School groups etc. Commissioner M. Webster shared the
Remind Application and how it functions and she was also familiar with GroupMe. I. Lam stated
she uses messenger but thinks RemindMe would work. President N. Quach thinks it would help
to send out invites in Google Calendar. He also mentioned sending out a copy of the Brown Act
to the new Commissioners to educate themselves on how it works. Commissioner M. Webster
asked about the Brown Act and the Commissioners, not missing meetings. Deputy Director B.
Houghton informed the Commission that absences are noted however the City as an entity
cannot remove a Commissioner only the Council Member who appointed them can remove
them from the Commission or it could also be a voluntary resignation. Deputy Director asked if
Remind has a Calendar option like Group Me. Commissioner Webster stated she doesn't believe
the Remind App has a calendar option. She also stated Google Calendar would be an attachment
to an email along with other links. Deputy Director B. Houghton stated we've had issues with
Google because the City emails because it's not Google platform based and that is why the issues
with Google Docs. Program Coordinator F. Reyes stated we'd see what options we have and
what works best for both the City and the Commission and report back.

Discussion of the Youth Summit
President N. Quach suggested they talk about the Youth Summit generally since they are new and
different Commissioners. He said they should talk about the future and the idea of a Youth
Summit and if they still like to do it. Commissioner M. Webster shared she had attended a
Women's conference with a variety of booths, guest speakers and information students would be
interested in.
 She stated she would enjoy having a Youth Summit as we move out of the Pandemic. President N.
Quach gave some context about the Youth Summit to the new Commissioners. He shared how
Advocacy was a big part of the planning of the Youth Summit. He asked the new Commissioners
what their general thought was on a Youth Summit and what would the's like to see be a part of a
Youth Summit. Commissioner I. Lam would be about teaching children about leadership and how
they had held an important position in their community. Commissioners A. Taing and C. You
agreed with the other Commissioners on what a Youth Summit would entail. Supervisor R. Rojas
said with the new commissioners it would be good to start over anew to make sure all
commissioners have input. She also mentioned setting a date a year from now and how meetings
and communication were important to reach their goals. Deputy Director B. Houghton shared
with the Commissioners we have a document to share with them to be used as a tool on "How to
Put on a Youth Summit". She shared how she wants them to have a Youth Summit to have their
voices heard and they'll be able to educate and motivate their peers. She explained how we need to
find the best form of communication to start planning. Program Coordinator F. Reyes agreed that
communication is key and that timelines with check-ins would be important to start building a
Youth Summit. President N. Quach shared how he was excited to come back and take time to plan
a Youth Summit.

Oral Communications
No orals at this time.

Commission Orals
Commissioner M. Webster welcomed the new commissioners. Commissioner C. Yu shared that
since it was his first day he has to get used to how meetings are run. Commissioner A. Tiang stated
he was excited to be a part of the Youth Commission and looking forward to working with the
Commission. Commissioner J. Quach welcomed the new commissioners. President N. Quach
echoed the welcoming of the new commissioners and stated how he was excited to work with
them. City staff introduced themselves to the new Youth Commission members.

Adjournment
President N. Quach motioned for adjournment at approximately 6:45 pm. It was motioned by
Commissioner J. Quach and seconded by Commissioner M. Webster.
